title: originSpiral respects the plot floor on torus and cone (F-10)
notes: lawSpiral (surface-fill-mono.js) advances a ring radius each step by wrapPitch(pitchFor(I), nz); wrapPitch folds that pitch to as little as 0.28x near the limb (nz -> 0), and on a torus/cone a much wider share of the front surface already rides that low-nz band (a cone's whole lateral face, a torus's inner rim) than on a sphere's thin rim, so the fold compounded with pitchFor's own deliberate sub-floor dark-tone pitch and collapsed ring-to-ring spacing under half a pen width: turns crossing under the pen, reading as moire/solid banding. Measured (per-angle radial gap, trace-instrumented): torus 518/4246 (12.2%) of on-surface gaps under 0.5x pen, cone 439/6344 (6.9%), sphere 815/31257 (2.6%, below the defect threshold, matching the finding's 'sphere reads correctly'). The fix floors the FOLDED pitch at 0.5x pen (Math.max(HALF_PEN, wrapPitch(...))) -- well below the full plot floor, so it clips only the samples already past the point of visibly crossing and leaves pitchFor's own dark-end headroom (the source of this law's 1.5x shadow/lit tonal contrast) untouched. Post-fix both torus and cone measured 0% under 0.5x pen. Visually: a before/after crop of the torus's foreshortened lower band shows the chevron interference pattern separating into distinct, evenly-gapped marks and the radiating limb lines gaining visible daylight between them (42531/320000 px changed on the hatch shot, 17385/418274 on the cone crosshatch shot). Switching the law's base pitch to pitchLegible (the full floor) instead was tried FIRST and REJECTED: it collapsed the tonal-range test's shadow/lit ratio from ~1.5 to 1.05 (bar 1.2) and the wrap test's rim/core ratio from 1.26 to 1.01 (bar 1.05) -- the deliberate sub-floor headroom IS the tonal contrast, and a blanket floor spends it everywhere, not just where it actually crosses.

tests.red: torus: ring-to-ring gap never crosses under half a pen width -- 518/4246 (12.2%) gaps under 0.5x pen on torus: expected 0.12199717381064532 to be less than or equal to 0.01; cone: 439/6344 (6.9%) gaps under 0.5x pen on cone: expected 0.06919924337957124 to be less than or equal to 0.01
tests.green: tests/unit/scene3d-origin-spiral-tonal-range.test.js: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 6 passed (6) -- includes the 2 new gap tests plus the pre-existing tonal-range/segment-count/weightScale tests, all still passing with their original margins

byte_identical_pairs: None. Sphere is NOT byte-identical: sphere already crossed the same half-pen line in 2.6% of on-surface gaps under the current test scene (deliberate sub-floor dark-end behaviour, shared by every primitive using pitchFor), so the same targeted clamp touches those samples too -- but ONLY those (0% below 0.5x pen post-fix, same as torus/cone), and both the pre-existing tonal-range test (1.5x contrast, bar 1.2) and wrap-foreshorten test (1.26x rim/core, bar 1.05) still pass with their original margins, which is this repo's own definition of 'the sphere reads correctly' for this law.
